flash.password_changed: Password changed. Other browsers must log in again.
flash.setup_done: Setup complete. Guests can now connect via Bluetooth.
headline.audio_disabled.detail: Phones can stay connected, but nothing is played on Lyrion.
headline.connected.detail: Press Play in any audio app on the phone.
headline.lyrion_unreachable.detail: Bluetooth stays connected; playback resumes when the server or player is back.
headline.not_configured.detail: Choose a Lyrion server and a player to finish setup.
headline.paused.detail: Playback resumes when Play is pressed on the phone.
headline.playing.detail: Bluetooth audio is playing on the selected Lyrion player.
headline.ready.detail: Waiting for a phone to connect.
headline.waiting_for_target.detail: Other music is playing on the player; the bridge does not interrupt it right now.
help.custom_key_pem: The private key is stored only on this device (readable by the service only).
help.device_name: The name guests see in their Bluetooth list and that this device shows in Home Assistant.
help.extra_hostnames: Further names that may be used to reach this device, e.g. a reverse-proxy name. Comma-separated.
help.https_only: Can only be switched on from an HTTPS connection, so you cannot lock yourself out.
help.local_hostname: Network name without “.local”, e.g. hifi-bridge → hifi-bridge.local.
help.mdns_backend: Avahi is preferred; the built-in responder is only used where no Avahi service runs.
help.mqtt_ca_pem: Only needed when the broker uses a certificate from your own CA. Verification is never switched off.
help.override_lms: If off, a phone never interrupts other music playing on the player.
help.pause_strategy: “Silence at once” stops the player within a fraction of a second when the phone pauses.
help.tls_mode: Local CA: the device issues its own certificate; install its CA once on your devices.
help.trusted_proxies: Only these addresses may tell the device the original client and protocol (X-Forwarded-*).
live.offline: Connection to the bridge lost – retrying …
live.pairing_open: Pairing open for {seconds} s – select “{name}” on the phone
login.help: Your browser can remember the owner password.
login.title: Log in
nav.label: Main navigation
pairing.guest_hint: Paired phones reconnect later without a pairing window.
pairing.help: Guests then select “{name}” in their phone’s Bluetooth settings – no app needed.
pairing.label: Name
pairing.one_source: Only one phone can play at a time; a second phone is refused and never interrupts the first.
pairing.open_for: Pairing open for {seconds} s – select “{name}” on the phone
pairing.remove.confirm: Remove this phone? It must pair again later.
refusal.lyrion_unreachable: Lyrion or the player is unreachable
settings.lyrion.help: Changing the server stops only the bridge’s own playback.
settings.mqtt.controls_help: Off by default: Home Assistant then only shows status. Each control is enabled separately; restrict access with broker ACLs.
settings.mqtt.help: Optional. Audio keeps working when the broker is down.
settings.playback.help: ICY titles stay off until older Squeezebox models are verified.
settings.token.help: Creates a new secret stream address. A running playback continues; new ones use the new address.
settings.token.title: Stream address
trust.android.2: Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate.
trust.android.3: Confirm the warning only after checking the fingerprint; then reopen the HTTPS address.
trust.intro: Your browser only shows the lock without warnings after you install this device’s own certificate authority (CA) once. It is valid only for local names (.local, .home.arpa, .lan, .internal) and private addresses – it cannot vouch for any website on the internet.
trust.ios.1: Open this page in Safari and download the .crt file; allow the profile download.
trust.ios.2: Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → install the profile.
trust.ios.3: Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings → enable full trust for “Hi-Fi Bridge local CA”.
trust.linux.1: Firefox: Settings → Privacy & Security → Certificates → View Certificates → Authorities → Import.
trust.linux.2: Tick “Trust this CA to identify websites”.
trust.linux.3: System-wide (Debian/Ubuntu): copy to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and run update-ca-certificates.
trust.macos.1: Download the .crt file and open it in Keychain Access (login keychain).
trust.macos.2: Double-click “Hi-Fi Bridge local CA” → Trust → “Always Trust”.
trust.macos.3: Close the window and confirm with your password.
trust.scope: The private key of this CA never leaves the device.
trust.title: Trust this device
trust.verify: Before trusting it, compare this fingerprint with the one shown during setup on the device (or later by the flash tool). Never accept a browser warning without this check.
trust.windows.1: Download the .crt file and open it.
trust.windows.2: Install certificate → Current user → place it in “Trusted Root Certification Authorities”.

wizard.bluetooth.title: Bluetooth name
wizard.code.help: The one-time setup code belongs to this device (development: file setup-code.txt in the data directory).

wizard.target.help: The bridge never creates or changes groups and never switches to another player on its own.

wizard.target.title: Player or group
wizard.target.unreachable: The Lyrion server is not reachable right now.
